findings.paper_evidence: PDF p. 3, printed p. 953 states Frobenius submultiplicativity as ||AB|| <= ||A||||B|| with only multiplication compatibility implicit; the surrounding norm discussion also uses rectangular matrices.
findings.lean_evidence: P15Matrix n is Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Real, and the target assigns this same type to both A and B.
findings.impact: The target omits every genuinely rectangular compatible product, so it is a nonvacuous but weaker specialization of the selected paper result.

rationale: The Lean target faithfully represents ordinary multiplication, the unsquared Frobenius norm, the constant-one non-strict inequality, and the paper's real-matrix context. Its sole material defect is dimensional: one common n forces both factors to be square, whereas the paper property applies to arbitrary multiplication-compatible shapes. Therefore the paper directly implies the Lean specialization, but the Lean proposition does not directly provide the paper's full claim.
